_comment: Assistant safety settings for Windows (macOS / Linux: settings.example.assistant.json; #281, #563: an assistant is a persistent session that reads the project and changes nothing in it, held by Claude Code's own permissions). Replace C:/ABSOLUTE/PATH with the absolute path of the project's core copy, <project>/coordinator/core (the folder that holds scripts/), written with FORWARD slashes (Claude Code runs hook commands through Git Bash, which drops backslashes; the guard is its .sh script, the one guard of every OS, #564), and C:/ABSOLUTE/PROJECT/coordinator/assistants/NAME with the assistant's folder (NAME: its name) in env COORD_ASSISTANT_DIR; the Edit rules write the same paths in Claude Code's POSIX form, the drive a lower-case letter after // (C:/x is //c/x; measured on 2.1.322: //C:/x matches nothing). defaultMode dontAsk (start-worker also starts an assistant with --permission-mode dontAsk): every tool call no allow rule names is refused at once, with no prompt - and the guard refuses an assistant's edit, Bash and PowerShell calls in any other mode. The base allow list is closed, reads only: Read, Grep, Glob; Edit (which covers Write, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit) inside the assistant's folder only; gh issue / pr / run / repo / project / search reads by fixed prefixes, the bare git branch and git config --get; SendMessage and ListAgents to talk to the coordinator; Claude Code's own read-only shell commands pass by its own check (measured on 2.1.322: ls, cat, and git status / log / diff / show / rev-parse in the session's folder, the project root; refused: git -C <dir> ..., cd <dir> && git ..., git --no-pager ..., git log --output=...), so git gets no wildcard rule beyond git config --get: a wildcard such as git -C * log would also match git -C . branch -D log. What one assistant's brief needs beyond it (a connector's read tools and the write tools its brief's write rule names, WebSearch, WebFetch per named domain, an outside folder the brief names) goes into that assistant's own allow list entry by entry, in the forms of _allow_per_brief, shown to the owner before the start; never a rule that can write or run code beyond what the brief names: no gh api, no git write form, no interpreter. A refusal in dontAsk invites another route, so the deny list names the writes besides: every git and GitHub write form an allow rule in another settings file (the user's own, the project's) could let through - a deny always wins - the whole PowerShell tool (an assistant reads through Bash), and the edit of the core copy, the assistants' settings, the project's .claude/ and ~/.claude/. A user-level allow rule still reaches an assistant for anything not denied here: keep the user's allow list free of writes, or deny them here too. worktree.bgIsolation none: the assistant works in its folder, not a worktree. MCP tools: the GitHub server's writes are denied by name (connected as "github": rename to this machine's server name); a connector's tools reach the assistant only through its allow list (_allow_per_brief). env COORD_PROTECTED_BRANCHES: as in settings.example.json (the guard's general rules still apply: a push to a protected branch is blocked). attribution hides the AI co-author trailer, the PR line and the session link (CORE section 11). The compact hook runs after-compact.ps1 assistant: after each compaction the assistant re-reads its own BRIEF.md and NOTES.md (COORD_ASSISTANT_DIR) and the core's roles/assistant.md. This file only - never the coordinator's own settings (TOOLKIT.md Safety, Assistants).
_allow_per_brief: The forms of what one assistant's BRIEF.md needs beyond the closed list (#563): the coordinator copies into permissions.allow only the entries that brief names, each written out, and shows the list to the owner before the start (the coord-assistant skill). Never a wildcard over a tool that writes or runs code.
mcp__SERVER__WRITE_TOOL - only a write tool the brief's write rule names; dontAsk gives no prompt, so draft-first rests on the assistant
WebFetch(domain:EXAMPLE.COM) - one entry per domain the brief names
Edit(//d/OUTSIDE/FOLDER/**) - an outside folder the brief names, the path written as the Edit rule above
